recommendation: Keep the audit as-is. Do not edit retired ProcedureRequest source or reintroduce fulfillment states into Request.status/ServiceRequest.status unless a later work-group decision reverses the workflow separation between authorization status and fulfillment status.
issue_request: FHIR-6877 observed that Procedure and ProcedureRequest status values overlapped and asked whether ProcedureRequest should replace completed with closed, remove in-progress/accepted-style fulfillment states, or add scheduled. The Published/Not Persuasive with Modification resolution directed alignment with workflow patterns through GF#10293/FHIR-10293.
initial_application: No source commit was found that directly names FHIR-6877. The linked Published FHIR-10293 workflow issue listed Procedure as an Event resource and ProcedureRequest as a Request resource, and its comments removed FHIR-6877 from the ballot-duplicate list after workflow changes were applied. Relevant source history includes fd96fa1d815117d335e22713f30f6792a9c83b1d applying Procedure workflow changes under #10293, e9a85998b0dbe25b03abd0045bfa30e67ce56b36 moving ProcedureRequest.status toward RequestStatus/request-status, and 06bd9f6ffe08096694a3424721006e5fdcd82d3a renaming ProcedureRequest to ServiceRequest.
additional_context: ProcedureRequest is out of the current build: source/fhir.ini actively lists Procedure and ServiceRequest and records ProcedureRequest only as merged into ServiceRequest. Current Request narrative explicitly separates requester-controlled status from fulfillment status, and related combined-branch audits for FHIR-11120 and FHIR-6876 reached the same request-status conclusion for the ProcedureRequest/ReferralRequest successor family.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current source already has Procedure.status bound to Event Status, ServiceRequest.status bound to Request Status, and Request pattern narrative stating that requested/accepted/in-progress fulfillment status is managed through Task/Event rather than Request.status.
